data.headline: Two-year Treasury yield falls to 4.76% as the curve steepens
data.summary: Treasury yields fell across the curve on Thursday. The two-year benchmark dropped four basis points and the 30-year benchmark fell one. That widened the gap between them to 64 basis points, from 61 on Wednesday.

bull.text: The ten-year yield fell three basis points to 5.04%. That lowered the Treasury benchmark used to price many new corporate bonds.

bear.text: Long-term borrowing remains relatively expensive. The 30-year Treasury yield ended Thursday at 5.40%.

watch.text: The two-year yield moved more than the 30-year on Thursday. The next Treasury release will show whether that difference persists.

limitations: The Treasury publishes estimated par yields. A business’s borrowing rate also depends on its credit spread.
